title: A MOST Framework Trial Evaluating the MOst effectiVe Exercise Types for Blood Pressure Control
official: A MOST Framework Trial Evaluating the MOst effectiVe Exercise Types for Blood Pressure Control
summary: Exercise is known to prevent nearly one in three cases of hypertension and slow its progression in young adults, but we do not know which specific exercise types are most effective. The main objective of this study is to determine which exercise prescription (ExRx) intervention component(s) alone or in combination most effectively lower systolic BP in young adults with stage I hypertension, identify the vascular mechanisms underlying these changes, and guide the development of optimized exercise-based prescription packages for effective hypertension control in this population.

interventions.name: Core intervention (Fitbit tracking and BP health education)

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 to 44 years
* Northwestern University patient with untreated Stage I hypertension (blood pressure 130-139/80-89 mmHg) documented on at least 2 outpatient encounters in the prior year
* No current antihypertensive medication use
* Estimated 10-year cardiovascular disease risk below 7.5% by the PREVENT risk calculator
* Body mass index 18.5 to 39.9 kg/m2
* Average home blood pressure of 130-139/80-89 mmHg during a 7-day home monitoring period
* Fewer than 150 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity measured by accelerometer
* Exercise readiness confirmed by the Physical Activity Readiness Questionnaire for Everyone (PAR-Q+), with medical clearance if indicated
* English fluency
* Reliable internet access on a computer, smartphone, or tablet, with videoconference capability (e.g., Zoom)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Use of a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) within the past year
* Weight change of more than 15 lbs in the prior 3 months
* Pregnant or planning to become pregnant within 6 months
* Active cancer and/or currently receiving cancer treatment
* History of type 1 or type 2 diabetes
* History of chronic kidney disease
* History of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
* History of cardiovascular disease or coronary heart disease
* Absolute contraindication to exercise (e.g., severe neurological, psychological, or orthopedic condition)
